findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed with accumulated debris:
- the shelves underneath the grill tops were heavily accumulated with spilled oils and food debris
- spaces in between standing coolers/freezers and other kitchen equipment were observed with dried grease debris
- the vent covers above the back prep station (near walk in cooler) were observed coated with dried debris. 
Ensure that non food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There was a build of grease and food debris observed on floors and walls throughout the kitchen area, mainly along the cook-line. The PIC is aware of the areas that are in need of cleaning and the facility is working to have the areas cleaned. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed several stacks of plates stored with the food contact surface faced upward (on storage shelf in dish room). Shown to PIC. Discussed that clean plates should be stored with the food contact surface inverted. Ensure that clean dishes are stored in a manner that prevent exposure of contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The lid of the prep cooler was observed in disrepair. It appeared that screws were missing from the lid. The prep cooler is along the line where the juice machine is stored. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that equipment is always in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed a container of raw beef to be stored above cooked breakfast sausages in the stacked freezer (across from cook-line). Discussed and shown to PIC and containers were rearranged. The beef was moved to the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below cooked ready-to-eat foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The vent covers above the back prep station area were observed with a significant amount of dust. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that the ventilation unit, along with the vent covers are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent possible contamination of food, as well as buildup of dust.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
A sanitizer bucket stored in the kitchen tested at 0ppm (q). The chemical wasn’t dispensing properly. PIC prepared a solution by mixing the chemical and water in a bucket. The facility will manually prepare sanitizer buckets until the dispenser is fixed to sanitize food contact surfaces and dishes will  be sanitized in the dish machine. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
A sheet of eggs stored in a cooler along the cookline tempted at 55F-60F. PIC mentioned that eggs were stored in the cooler since late morning. The eggs were moved to another cooler on the cookline. Be sure that TCS food items are held at 41F or below to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
A cooler along the cook-line appears to not be functioning properly. The cooler was storing eggs that were tempting between 55F-60F. Discussed with PIC and maintenance will be contacted to service the cooler. Ensure that coolers are working properly and sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow-up on this. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed rinsing hands in the dump sink. There is signage posted above the dump sink noting that the sink is to only be used for dumping liquids. Discussed with PIC to educate state on proper sink usage. Ensure that employees are cleaning hands in hand washing sinks only. 

2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed a cutting board to be stored in close proximity to a handsink. The cutting board was stored on a hook to the left of the handwashing sink. Discussed with PIC and cutting board was removed. Ensure that cutting boards are always stored in a manner that prevents contamination and exposure of  splatter.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The surface underneath the fryers (small fryers) was observed to be heavily soiled with food debris and accumulated grease. Discussed with PIC techniques to clean underneath fryers due to the inability to move the pieces of equipment. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
